---
title: "Plant phenology"
---

iNaturalist observers can annotate a plant observation as *Flower Budding*,
*Flowering*, *Fruiting*, or *No Evidence of Flowering*. Only a small share of plant
observations carry one of these annotations, so this page looks at a short list of
common species in Maryland, Pennsylvania, and DC, pulled through the API with
`scripts/pull_phenology.R`.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(lubridate)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
month_breaks <- c(1, 5, 9, 14, 18, 22, 27, 31, 35, 40, 44, 48)
phases <- c("Flower Budding", "Flowering", "Fruiting", "No Evidence of Flowering")

ann <- read_csv(here("data", "processed", "phenology_annotations.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    observed_on = as.Date(observed_on),
    week        = pmin(isoweek(observed_on), 52L),
    biweek      = (week - 1L) %/% 2L * 2L + 1L,
    phenophase  = factor(phenophase, levels = phases),
    label       = coalesce(common_name, species)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(observed_on), !is.na(phenophase))
```

## Coverage

```{r coverage}
ann |>
  count(label, state) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = state, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(desc(rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Flowering windows

For each species and state, the dot is the median week of observations annotated
*Flowering* and the bar spans the 10th to 90th percentile. Only species and state
combinations with at least 30 flowering annotations are shown.

```{r windows}
#| fig-height: 7
windows <- ann |>
  filter(phenophase == "Flowering") |>
  group_by(label, status, state) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            p10 = quantile(week, 0.10),
            median = median(week),
            p90 = quantile(week, 0.90),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 30)

windows |>
  mutate(label = fct_reorder(label, median, .fun = median)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = label, x = median, xmin = p10, xmax = p90, colour = state)) +
  geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = month_breaks, labels = month.abb) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

```{r windows-table}
windows |>
  arrange(median) |>
  transmute(Species = label, Status = status, State = state,
            `Flowering obs` = n,
            `Median date` = format(as.Date("2025-01-01") + (median - 1) * 7, "%b %d"),
            `10th pct` = format(as.Date("2025-01-01") + (p10 - 1) * 7, "%b %d"),
            `90th pct` = format(as.Date("2025-01-01") + (p90 - 1) * 7, "%b %d")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Phenophase mix through the year

Share of annotated observations in each phenophase by two-week bin, all three
jurisdictions pooled. Species with fewer than 60 annotations are left out.

```{r mix}
#| fig-height: 9
keep_species <- ann |> count(label) |> filter(n >= 60) |> pull(label)

ann |>
  filter(label %in% keep_species) |>
  count(label, biweek, phenophase) |>
  ggplot(aes(biweek, n, fill = phenophase)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = month_breaks, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of annotated observations", fill = NULL)
```

## Caveats

- Annotations are added by observers and identifiers, not collected systematically.
  People tend to photograph and annotate flowers more than leaves or bare stems, so
  "Flowering" is over-represented relative to how long a plant is actually in flower.
- Windows from observations describe when plants are *seen* flowering, which lags the
  true start and end of flowering, especially for rarely observed species.
- Years are pooled. A natural next step is to compare windows across years and against
  spring temperature to look for shifts.
